title: UK and Singapore Align on Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration and Quantum Security Standards in Financial Sector - Quantum Computing Report
gist: At the 11th UK-Singapore Financial Dialogue, MAS, HM Treasury, the Bank of England and the FCA agreed to deepen cooperation on quantum security and banks' migration to quantum-safe systems, combining NCSC PQC migration guidance with findings from MAS's QKD sandbox. Regulators told banks to run immediate cryptographic discovery audits, and both countries will use the UK's 2027 G20 Presidency and Singapore's ASEAN Chairmanship to push international quantum cyber-resilience standards.

insights.claim: At the 11th UK-Singapore Financial Dialogue, MAS, HM Treasury, the Bank of England and the FCA agreed to deepen bilateral cooperation on quantum security, supervisory expectations and the banking sector's transition to quantum-safe systems.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum risk is now on major regulators' supervisory agenda; expect compliance-driven PQC spending by banks.

insights.claim: Joint oversight by MAS, HMT, BoE and FCA aims to set unified regulatory standards for commercial banks and capital-market participants adopting quantum-safe technology.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Harmonized supervisory standards would turn PQC migration from optional to mandated for regulated firms.

insights.claim: Regulators stressed that commercial banks must conduct immediate cryptographic discovery audits to identify legacy dependencies before utility-scale quantum systems emerge.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Near-term demand driver for crypto-inventory and PQC migration tooling vendors serving financial institutions.
insights.quote: commercial banks must conduct immediate cryptographic discovery audits to identify legacy dependencies before utility-scale quantum systems emerge

themes.theme: PQC migration and QKD sandbox inputs

insights.claim: The UK presented NCSC migration guidance outlining phased timelines for deploying quantum-resistant public-key algorithms and phasing out vulnerable RSA and elliptic-curve cryptography in core banking applications.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: NCSC timelines set the pace for UK banks' PQC replacement cycles.

insights.claim: MAS shared findings from its industry QKD sandbox, run with commercial banks and telecom operators, which tested physical-layer quantum key exchange on live financial transaction rails and produced data on interoperability, hardware costs and network overhead.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Singapore is the leading regulator testing QKD in finance; cost/overhead data will shape whether banks adopt hardware QKD versus software PQC.

insights.claim: Quantum security was a dedicated focus even though the dialogue also covered digital asset tokenization, agentic AI governance and capital markets reform.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum risk is treated as systemic alongside tokenization and AI on regulators' agendas.

insights.claim: With the UK holding the G20 Presidency and Singapore the ASEAN Chairmanship in 2027, both agreed to coordinate their leadership roles to promote international standards for quantum cyber resilience; the 12th dialogue will be hosted by the UK in 2027.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Possible G20-level quantum-safe finance agenda in 2027 could accelerate global PQC mandates.
insights.locator: With the UK assuming the G20 Presidency
